page: Microsoft Azure D2nls_v6 is an entry-level virtual machine within the low-memory Dnlv6 series. Powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance runs on a dedicated x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz. The hardware allocation includes two vCPUs mapped to a single physical core via hyper-threading, supported by 48 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a shared 260 MB L3 cache. System memory is constrained to 4.0 GB of RAM, resulting in a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance includes no local storage or bundled public IPv4 addresses, relying on external Premium Storage for disk operations, and does not feature GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations indicate mixed execution characteristics driven by the single physical core configuration. Single-core performance remains competitive, with stress-ng single-core compute, gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression ranking in the average middle tier. However, multi-core capacity and aggregate throughput are constrained, placing stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU ratings in the lower quartiles. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth of 15.54 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 11.76 GB/sec reflect the entry-level memory sub-system. In application-level testing, Redis SET throughput reached 2.28 million operations per second and static web serving delivered 3.59 GB/sec.

From an infrastructure perspective, the D2nls_v6 offers a low entry cost for workloads that demand modern instruction set extensions such as AVX-512, AMX, and AES without requiring large memory allocations. The primary tradeoff lies in the shared physical core architecture and 4.0 GB RAM boundary, which restricts multi-threaded scaling and memory-resident tasks. This instance is suitable for lightweight network-optimized tasks, microservices, low-traffic web serving, small CI/CD automation workers, and basic utility services.
description: Microsoft Azure D2nls_v6 is a low-memory, compute-oriented instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Equipped with two vCPUs across one physical hyper-threaded core and 4.0 GB of system memory, it provides a compact 1:2 core-to-RAM ratio. The server lacks integrated local disk storage and GPU hardware, depending on network-attached storage for persistence. In performance testing, the instance exhibits solid single-threaded execution, supported by AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets, but multi-core throughput and memory bandwidth are bounded by the two-vCPU footprint. With 3.59 GB/sec in static web throughput and moderate database operation ratings, it represents a cost-effective, stripped-down node for lightweight microservices, front-end proxies, and low-concurrency network tasks.
